title: Hadamard-coded tier reads give gain-cell stacks a multiplex advantage
idea: Borrow Fellgett's multiplex advantage from Hadamard spectroscopy: instead of one tier at a time, drive the read wordlines of 16 capacitorless 2T0C gain-cell tiers sharing one vertical read bitline with Hadamard S-matrix patterns over 16 slots, digitize the summed current, and invert the matrix to recover all 16 bits. The ~2-4x SNR gain lets read transistors be weak deposited channels and amortizes one ADC over 16 tiers.
why: No capacitor; Fact 7 (periphery) and tolerance of low-mobility tiers; 16 bits per read burst.

title: Echo-located cells: time-domain reflectometry addresses tiers on slow-wave lines
idea: Make each vertical read line a slow-wave transmission line (high-k loaded and meandered, ~1/50 c) on which each capacitorless floating-body or gain cell presents a state-dependent impedance bump. A 20 ps pulse is launched and the echo arrival time says which tier answered while its amplitude gives the bit, so a whole string is read in one trace with no tier decoder, staircase or per-tier select line.
why: Fact 2 (3D addressing overhead) and Fact 7: tier select logic disappears; timing resolution makes it speculative.

title: Lock-in dithered read pulls gain-cell bits from 1,024-cell strings
idea: Read like a lock-in amplifier: superimpose a small 500 MHz dither on the selected gain cell's read wordline so only that cell's current is modulated, and synchronously demodulate the shared bitline at that frequency, rejecting DC leakage from 1,023 unselected capacitorless cells. Non-destructive, background-rejecting reads let one sense channel serve a 1,024-cell vertical string spanning many tiers.
why: Fact 7 (49% periphery) and leakage-limited string length: ~4-8x fewer sense channels; no capacitor.

title: Coincidence-counter logic: triple-gate cells answer only to x, y, z
idea: Particle detectors accept events only on triple coincidence; build a cubic 3D lattice in which every capacitorless floating-body cell has three series gates, one on each of three orthogonal line families entering from three faces of the block, so it conducts only when all three are pulsed. Any cell in an N x N x N block is selected with 3N drivers (3,000 for a billion cells) instead of per-tier decoders and a staircase.
why: Fact 2 and Fact 7: addressing hardware scales as 3N rather than N^2 per tier; no capacitor; triple-gate cell fabrication is the risk.

title: MRI slice-select: voltage gradient picks one tier via anti-ambipolar cells
idea: MRI selects a slice with a gradient plus a narrow-band pulse; electrically, pass current through a resistive vertical gate pillar so gate voltage falls linearly across 64 tiers, and use access devices with a Lambda-shaped (anti-ambipolar p-n heterojunction) transfer curve that conduct only inside a ~100 mV window. Shifting the pillar's offset slides the conducting slice to the chosen tier, with storage on a capacitorless gain node and no per-tier select lines, Vt coding or staircase.
why: Fact 2: one driver per pillar replaces tier decoding; no capacitor; window sharpness across 64 tiers is the risk.

title: Spectral photoconductance metrology becomes color-addressed bandgap-graded tiers
idea: To probe buried tiers individually, grade Ge content so each tier's SiGe absorbs its own NIR band and probe with tunable light; then reuse the trick as tier select: each tier's capacitorless gain cell has a photo-gated access device responding only to its band, fed by a backside waveguide grid, while bitlines run through all tiers.
why: Fact 2: removes staircase and tier decoders (16 tiers by 16 wavelengths); no capacitor; optical power and speed are the risks.

title: Self-referenced reads tolerate 200 mV tier variability in cheap gain-cell stacks
idea: Borrow MRAM's self-reference measurement: read a capacitorless gain cell's current, write a known 1, read again, compare in a local sample-and-hold, then restore, so each cell is its own reference. Deposited low-temperature poly-Si or oxide tiers with +/-200 mV Vt spread, which no fixed reference can sense, become usable without monocrystalline layer transfer.
why: Fact 2 cost of 3D tiers: cheap deposited tiers instead of epitaxial or bonded ones, paid with ~2x read latency; no capacitor.

title: Heterodyne addressing: row-column tone mixing reads selectorless crosspoint tiers
idea: From intermodulation spectroscopy: drive every row of a stacked crosspoint with its own tone f_i and every column with g_j; only cells whose rectification is switched on (bistable ferroelectric-semiconductor Schottky diodes such as alpha-In2Se3, no capacitor) generate the f_i+g_j mixing product. One spectral readout of the summed current reports a whole sub-array, and linear sneak paths produce no tones at those frequencies.
why: Removes selectors and per-row sense amps for dense crosspoint tiers (Facts 2 and 7); SNR and mixing efficiency are speculative.

title: Charge-division readout: two-ended ratio proves which tier actually answered
idea: Position-sensitive detectors locate a hit by the current ratio at the two ends of a resistive strip; make each vertical read line of a capacitorless gain-cell stack deliberately resistive and sense it at top and bottom, so the ratio encodes which tier conducted while the sum gives the bit. Every read self-verifies its tier address, catching decoder faults and wrong-tier activation in 100+ tier stacks without extra ECC bits.
why: Fact 2 reliability: silent wrong-tier reads are a new 3D failure mode; verification lets decoder margins relax; no capacitor.

title: Grain-mapped maskless placement puts every access device inside one grain
idea: After a solid-phase-crystallized silicon tier is deposited, a fast electron-channeling or polarized-light imager maps every grain boundary on the wafer in minutes; a multi-beam maskless writer then shifts each capacitorless gain-cell transistor's active area by up to +/-100 nm so it sits inside a single grain. The base die stores the per-die placement map.
why: Fact 2: near-single-crystal device quality from cheap deposited tiers, no bonding or crucible-grown donor; ~10x lower Vt spread than random poly.

title: Resonance-read buckled nanobeams: contact-free bistable bits in stacked cavities
idea: MEMS sensors read state as a resonance shift; store each bit as the up or down buckling of a ~200 nm compressively stressed AlN/SiN nanobeam in a sealed cavity per tier, snapped electrostatically in ~5 ns without touching any electrode, so there is no stiction wear-out. An asymmetric AlN layer makes the two states resonate ~15% apart, read non-destructively by the beam's own piezoelectric transduction.
why: No capacitor, no refresh (bistable), contact-free flipping for unlimited endurance, stackable cavity tiers; density and speed are speculative.

title: Diamond NV imaging verifies vertical racetracks threading through tier stacks
idea: Widefield NV-diamond magnetometry can image domain walls inside buried wires; with that metrology loop, line deep holes through a deposited stack with Co/Ni multilayer magnetic racetracks storing 64 domains each, shifted by spin-orbit current pulses past one MTJ read/write head at the hole top. The bit is a magnetic domain, not charge, so no capacitor or refresh is needed.
why: No capacitor, unlimited shift endurance, hole-array density at ~10-50 ns access; shift reliability is speculative.

title: Piezoresistive read of remanent ferroelastic strain stores bits without charge
idea: Strain-gauge metrology inspires the cell: a thin ferroelastic layer (twin-switchable BiFeO3 or a shape-memory film) flips between two remanent strain states under a gate field, and that strain changes a Si nanosheet channel's resistance by ~30% through piezoresistance. Reading is non-destructive and the state holds without stored charge, so tiers stack with no capacitor or refresh.
why: No capacitor, no refresh (Fact 3), non-destructive read (Fact 8); ferroelastic switching endurance is speculative.

title: PFM-discovered conductive domain walls become stacked lithium-niobate tier switches
idea: Piezoresponse force microscopy revealed that charged domain walls in LiNbO3 conduct; in thin-film LNOI tiers a write pulse creates or erases a conductive wall between two lateral electrodes, and a low-voltage read senses wall conduction without reversing polarization. The stored state is the wall itself, not a capacitor.
why: No capacitor, non-destructive read, ns switching and >1e10 cycles reported in bulk; wall retention at 10 nm scale is the risk.

title: XMLD-proven Neel switching builds stray-field-free antiferromagnetic tiers
idea: X-ray magnetic linear dichroism imaging proved current pulses rotate the Neel vector in CuMnAs and Mn2Au; build capacitorless cells where an in-plane current pulse through an antiferromagnetic bar writes the bit and an antiferromagnetic or altermagnetic tunnel junction (Mn3Sn, RuO2) reads it. With no stray field, cells pack below 20 nm pitch and stack in tiers without the magnetic crosstalk that limits 3D MRAM.
why: No capacitor or refresh, unlimited endurance, dense stacking; read signal size is a high physics risk.

title: Write-current signature monitor ends each capacitorless write early
idea: Instrument the write driver of floating-body or thyristor 3D cells with a fast current-derivative detector that recognizes the impact-ionization or latch-on knee marking a completed state change, and cut the pulse within ~1 ns of it. Slow tiers get longer pulses and fast tiers stop early, so the design no longer pads every write for the slowest tier.
why: 3D energy and variability: ~40-60% lower write energy and ~2x lower average write latency across 100+ tiers; no capacitor.

title: JEDEC test suite for capacitorless cells written before products exist
idea: Measurement-first standardization: U.S. buyers and labs define the qualification metrics a capacitorless DRAM-class cell must pass (read disturb per 1e15 reads, cross-tier write disturb, retention tail under hammer, VRT incidence) and publish reference test patterns and limits. Hyperscalers can then qualify gain-cell, thyristor or floating-body memory without DDR spec assumptions built around capacitors.
why: Strategy: removes the qualification barrier that keeps capacitorless memories out of servers and shortens time-to-market for U.S. entrants.

title: Per-tier Kelvin-probe work-function readings tune gate alloy layer by layer
idea: After each monolithic tier's channel is deposited, a contactless corona-Kelvin probe maps its flat-band voltage, and the next gate deposition co-sputters a TiN/TiAl ratio chosen to cancel that tier's measured Vt shift, since lower tiers see extra anneals. A 32-tier capacitorless gain-cell stack lands every tier within ~+/-20 mV without implants or tier-specific bias rails.
why: Fact 2 tier uniformity: ~3-5x tighter cross-tier Vt and narrower sense margins; no capacitor.

title: Embedded thermal-witness markers record every tier's real anneal history
idea: Place witness structures in each tier (dopant diffusion couples and a phase-change alloy that crystallizes at a known time-temperature) whose sheet resistance, read at sort, reports the thermal budget that tier actually saw. Monolithic capacitorless gain-cell tiers over logic can then use ~50-75 C hotter spike anneals wherever witnesses show margin, instead of guard-banding every tier to a blanket 400 C limit.
why: Fact 2: better channels and contacts in upper monolithic tiers while protecting logic below; no capacitor.

title: Stochastic-depth contacts plus measured landing map replace the 3D staircase
idea: Etch all tier contacts in one step with a spread of hole diameters so aspect-ratio-dependent etch lands them across tiers, about 3 holes per tier; an electrical sort routine then pulses each tier's sacrificial ID line, detects which contacts answer, and stores the contact-to-tier map in the base die. No staircase trims or per-tier masks are needed, and redundant landings absorb etch variation in capacitorless gain-cell tiers.
why: Facts 2 and 4: the staircase eats die area and many trim-etch steps; one litho step plus measurement replaces it.

title: On-die moire offset sensor enables electronic alignment of fine-pitch tier bonds
idea: Every bonded capacitorless memory tier carries clusters of 9 sub-micron pads per signal plus an IR-readable moire offset sensor; after coarse +/-1 um die-to-wafer placement, the sensor reports the true offset and per-cluster switches route each signal through whichever pad pair overlaps. Connection pitch stays ~1 um while placement tolerance relaxes tenfold, with no mechanical correction.
why: 3D bonding cost: ~10x faster low-precision placement tools with fine-pitch connectivity; no capacitor.
